facility_roles.quote: The CONNIE detector is an array of 14 charge-coupled devices (CCDs) operating at the Angra 2 reactor of the Almirante Alvaro Alberto Nuclear Power Plant, in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

intervals.label: engineering run with a 4 g prototype
intervals.note: Year precision for the start ("late 2014"); the end is the full sensor upgrade in "mid 2016" (next interval). The engineering run paper (arXiv:1604.01343) reports the first year of operation of the 4 g prototype.
intervals.quote: The engineering prototype of the experiment was installed at the reactor site in late 2014

intervals.label: data taking with the upgraded CCD array
intervals.note: Open-ended: later papers report 2019 data and a skipper-CCD update (2021-22, conference abstract only), and the 2022 paper says the experiment "is taking data". No source consulted states that data taking has ended.
intervals.quote: A complete upgrade of the sensors was performed in mid 2016

physics_goals.quote: with the goal of measuring low-energy recoils from coherent elastic scattering (CE$\nu$NS) of reactor antineutrinos with silicon nuclei and testing nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI)
physics_goals.value: Measure low-energy recoils from coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering of reactor antineutrinos on silicon with CCDs, and test non-standard neutrino interactions

summary.plain: An array of very low-noise silicon camera chips (CCDs) 30 metres from the Angra 2 nuclear reactor in Brazil, built to spot the tiny recoil of a silicon nucleus when a reactor antineutrino scatters off it coherently. It has set limits and continues to improve its sensitivity.
summary.technical: Coherent Neutrino-Nucleus Interaction Experiment: low-noise fully depleted CCDs (8-14 devices, 47.6 g active in 2016, 36.2 g fiducial in 2019) at 30 m from the 3.8 GW_th Angra 2 core, surface, passive polyethylene/lead shield; reactor-on minus reactor-off spectra with ~50-1000 eV thresholds set limits 40-66 x the Standard Model CEvNS rate; 2021-22 skipper-CCD upgrade.
